# Bureau v2: product spec (source of truth)

## One line
Set up once, start a campaign, and walk away. Until the campaign ends, Bureau finds every relevant job it can reach, picks the ones worth applying to (including stretch roles), writes a truthful, tailored, human-sounding application for each, submits it on the employer's own form or by email, learns new forms as it goes, follows up, and reports, with no human approval in the loop.

## The owner's strategy (the writer and matcher must serve it)
Entry-level postings list far more than the job needs. The hard part is landing the interview, not learning the skill. So Bureau applies to roles **even when the candidate doesn't meet every listed requirement**, presents the candidate's real experience in the strongest honest light, and when a company shows interest it gives the candidate a crash plan to learn the gaps before the interview.

The line Bureau never crosses: it doesn't claim skills, experience, employers, numbers or credentials the candidate doesn't have. Fabrication gets caught at the technical screen or background check, after the interview has already been won, so it destroys the exact thing this strategy fights for. Honest stretch framing is the method (see Writer).

## The parts
1. **Onboarding and profile.** CV upload (exists). Links: GitHub, portfolio, LinkedIn URL, socials. A **voice bank**: 6–10 short passages the candidate writes in their own words (why they build, proudest project story, a hard problem solved, what they're learning now, the kind of team they want). An **answer bank** of standing answers to common form questions. A **learning list** (skills currently being learned). The profile auto-refreshes daily from new CV uploads, GitHub repos/READMEs/commits and the portfolio site. Every fact keeps its source.
2. **Scout.** Pulls the maximum reachable set of relevant postings every 2–3 hours from every legitimate source: company ATS feeds (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, SmartRecruiters, Workday, Workable, Recruitee, Personio, Teamtailor, BambooHR, Breezy and more), aggregators through the JobSpy sidecar (LinkedIn/Indeed/Glassdoor/Google/ZipRecruiter/Naukri/Bayt guest search), remote boards, community threads (HN, Reddit), local boards (Rozee.pk, Mustakbil, Bayt, GulfTalent, NaukriGulf where reachable), Claude deep web search, and manual capture. It keeps a **company registry** that grows by itself through ATS auto-detection and discovery. It resolves every listing to the employer's own apply URL, merges duplicates across sources (fingerprint plus embeddings), filters ghost and scam listings, and prioritises freshness (first 48 hours). It also tracks **hiring signals** (sudden rises in a company's open roles, funding news) to find roles before they're widely posted.
3. **Matcher.** Hard filters (location, remote, visa, salary floor, exclusions, company cooldown). Then embedding similarity. Then a Claude assessment whose score means **"how likely the candidate is to pass the screen"**, not "ticks every box". Requirements are split into critical, important and nice. Unmet *nice* requirements barely matter. Unmet *important* requirements are allowed up to the campaign's **stretch level** (conservative / balanced / aggressive). Unmet *critical* requirements that are true blockers (legally required licence, clearance, citizenship, a degree mandated by law, or years of experience far out of reach) cap the score.
4. **Writer.** For each selected job it produces a tailored CV PDF, cover letter, email subject line, form short-answers and an outreach note. Pipeline: decode the posting → research the company → build an **evidence map** (requirement → the best true evidence → framing: direct / transferable / learning / omit) → assemble the CV (their vocabulary for true skills, relevance ordering, and a *Currently learning* section drawn only from the learning list) → generate three letter variants built by **editing and adapting the candidate's own voice-bank writing** (research shows AI-*edited* human text is far harder to tell from human writing than AI-*generated* text) → a recruiter-critic picks the best → humanizer passes (Wikipedia "Signs of AI writing" patterns plus anti-slop rules) → a stylometric lint (sentence-length spread, lexical diversity band, banned phrases, cliché openers and closers, em-dash and rule-of-three limits) → the truth lock (code check plus independent auditor) → done. Gaps are named honestly and turned into proof of fast learning. Reply rates by variant style feed back into future choices.
5. **Form engine.** Detects which ATS a form runs on, extracts every field (including shadow DOM, iframes, custom comboboxes, date pickers, location typeaheads, repeating sections and multi-step wizards), maps each field to a value source (profile / answer bank / writer / file) with confidence, fills it with widget-specific handlers, **reads back and verifies** before submit, submits, and confirms. Known forms run from **recipes** (declarative JSON fill plans) and per-ATS adapters. When a selector breaks, it repairs itself by semantic matching, then hands over to the browser agent. It handles account creation and email verification codes for ATSs that need a login (Workday, iCIMS, Taleo, SuccessFactors) using a dedicated job-search mailbox and vault-stored per-site passwords. Unknown required questions it can't answer truthfully → skip the job, save the question, ask the owner in the digest, add the answer to the bank, and re-queue.
6. **Browser agent and learning.** For forms with no recipe, a Claude-driven browser agent fills the form using the accessibility tree plus screenshots, inside strict guardrails (allowed domains, step budget, no payments, no CAPTCHA solving, stop before submit, then the verifier). Every action is recorded as a **trace**. A compiler turns successful traces into recipes, shadow-verifies them on later runs, and promotes them after three matching runs. Learning one Workday form covers every company on Workday.
7. **External agent API and MCP.** Other agents (Muse, Claude in Chrome or any browser agent) can use Bureau: search jobs, pull an application packet (CV PDF, letter, answers), ask for the answer to any form question, fetch a recipe, report traces and mark a job submitted with proof. API keys with scopes, rate limits and an audit log. Exposed as REST (`/api/v1`) and as an MCP server (stdio plus streamable HTTP). External traces teach the system too, after shadow verification.
8. **Campaign autopilot.** A campaign has a start and end, roles/categories, locations, stretch level, minimum score, daily cap, per-company cooldown, active hours with human-like pacing and jitter, an AI budget cap, a dry-run period, and sources and channels. It runs unattended across restarts and auto-stops at the end date. Kill switch from the UI, Telegram `/stop` or a flag file. A job pipeline state machine ensures nothing is double-applied.
9. **Inbox and follow-up.** A dedicated mailbox over IMAP. It classifies every message (rejection / interview / assessment / recruiter question / verification code / other), links it to the application and updates its stage. Verification codes go to the form engine. Interviews and assessments trigger an instant Telegram alert. It sends one polite follow-up after N days when a hiring contact is known. It never auto-replies to interview scheduling: that alerts the owner.
10. **Learning engine.** When an interview or assessment arrives, a crash learning plan for that company's gaps and stack (day by day, with resources and a mini project). A weekly skill-gap report shows the most-missed skills across all scored jobs and suggests weekend projects that turn gaps into real CV lines. Optional auto-accept of top gaps into the learning list (owner opt-in, off by default).
11. **Reporting.** A daily digest by Telegram and email: sent (with screenshots in the UI), skipped with reasons, needs-you items, new questions for the answer bank, spend, interviews, top gaps. Live activity in the UI.
12. **UI.** Onboarding wizard, campaigns, pipeline, writer studio, forms and recipes, agents and API keys, inbox, learning, sources and companies, digest history, settings. Responsive and installable on a phone (PWA), in the Cream & Crimson design system.

## Quality bars
- **Scout:** ≥ 2,000 unique relevant postings per day across sources once the registry is seeded, with per-source health shown in the UI.
- **Writer:** every letter passes the stylometric lint and the truth lock; recruiter-critic score ≥ 8/10, or the job is skipped.
- **Forms:** ≥ 95% verified-fill success on fixtures for every adapter. Live success rate tracked per ATS.
- **Autopilot:** zero double applications, zero submissions with unverified fields, and graceful resume after a crash or reboot.
